TRIN 101.name: Comparative Grammar (English-Turkish)
TRIN 101.description: Comparative study of the principal grammatical structures of English and Turkish, including lexical items. Presentation of basic concepts necessary for lexical studies: semantics, etymology, variants and formation.

TRIN 102.name: Applied Linguistics
TRIN 102.description: Introduction to applied linguistics with special emphasis on the morphological, syntax and semantics of the French and Turkish languages. Role of linguistics in translation and in rhetoric analysis.

TRIN 103.name: Comparative Grammar (French-Turkish)
TRIN 103.description: Comparative study of the principal grammatical structures of French and Turkish, including lexical items. Presentation of basic concepts necessary for lexical study: semantics, etymology, variants and formation.

TRIN 111.name: Current Affairs for Translators in French
TRIN 111.description: This course consists of an introduction to theory and methods of translation. It includes a study of the nature, function and features of language, a survey of development of French, and a description of translation as a profession.

TRIN 112.name: French Turkish Translation
TRIN 112.description: This course consists of translation from French into Turkish of topics drawn from a variety of sources. The course includes comparative stylistics of French and Turkish, including a study of language registers. It also includes the use of recorded broadcasts and radio reports as a spoken source for translation and interpretation purposes.

TRIN 121.name: Introduction to Translation in English
TRIN 121.description: This course consists of an introduction to theory and methods of translation. It includes a study of the nature, function and features of language, a survey of development of English, and a description of translation as a profession.

TRIN 122.name: English-Turkish Translation
TRIN 122.description: This course consists of oral and written translation from English into Turkish of topics drawn from a variety of sources. The course includes comparative stylistics of English and Turkish, including a study of language registers. It also includes the use of recorded broadcasts and radio reports as a spoken source for translation and interpretation purposes.

TRIN 133.name: Texts and Composition in French I
TRIN 133.description: This course uses texts of a general nature as a basis for developing the students' oral and written skills in French. Emphasis is on style, language registers, vocabulary building and composition. Oral work includes small group discussions and debates on current topics in addition to public speaking.

TRIN 134.name: Texts and Composition in French II
TRIN 134.description: This course uses texts of a general nature as a basis for developing the students' oral and written skills in French. Emphasis is on style, language registers, vocabulary building and composition. Oral work includes small group discussions and debates on current topics in addition to public speaking.

TRIN 161.name: Introduction to Translation
TRIN 161.description: This course consists of an introduction to the theory and methods of translation. It includes a study of the nature, function and features of language, a survey of the development of the English, French and Turkish languages, and a description of translation as a profession.

TRIN 166.name: English-Turkish-French Translation
TRIN 166.description: This course consists of oral and written translation from English into Turkish and from French into Turkish of topics drawn from a variety of sources. The course includes comparative stylistics of English / Turkish and French / Turkish, including a study of language registers. It also includes the use of recorded broadcasts and radio reports as a spoken source for translation purposes.

TRIN 172.name: Computer Literacy
TRIN 172.description: Basic Computer Literacy. Efficient use of a computer for translation students, using word processing, compression, web page building, presentation, picture, spreadsheet and database software.

TRIN 191.name: Turkish for Translators
TRIN 191.description: The course consists of information on the general characteristics of the Turkish language. The emphasis is on the speaking and diction strategy. This course particularly stresses the need to speak Turkish efficiently and correctly with a special emphasis on the right pronunciation of words.

TRIN 205.name: English-American and French Culture
TRIN 205.description: The study of contemporary American and French societies through a selection of texts and audiovisual materials. Emphasis on the cultural, social and legal aspects of American and French civilization.

TRIN 207.name: Language of Journalism
TRIN 207.description: An analytical approach to the study of journalistic texts (French or English and Turkish). Emphasis is on journalistic style and register.

TRIN 212.name: Technology for Translators
TRIN 212.description: Use of technologies, online tools by translators. Use of machine assisted translation with pre- and post- editing procedures. Use of contemporary computer assisted translation tools. Study and application of CAT. Use of subtitling technologies. Formulation of online translator friendly terminology data bases. Student led presentations and group projects.

TRIN 221.name: Translation Studies I
TRIN 221.description: The aim of the course is to discuss evolving and developing translation theories starting from Babel. This course provides insight about the "translation traditions" of different countries at different times in history and equips students with the mental flexibility needed to question and investigate the relationship between theory and practice.

TRIN 222.name: Translation Studies II
TRIN 222.description: Translation Studies II is follow-up course of Translation Studies I. The aim of the course is to discuss evolving and developing translation theories starting from the postmodern era until today. The course provides insight about the "translation traditions" of different countries at different times in history and equips students with the mental flexibility needed to question and investigate the relationship between theory and practice.

TRIN 227.name: British and American Cultures and Civilisations
TRIN 227.description: The aim of the course is to introduce Anglo-Saxon culture and civilisation via texts and speeches. Various text types will be analysed to create awareness about shifting from source culture to target culture. Comparative studies will be carried out in order to be successful in translation applications. It will be based on current culturel events and texts. Selected examples from historical literary and daily life habits.

TRIN 228.name: French Culture and Civilisation
TRIN 228.description: The aim of the course is to introduce French culture and civilisation via texts and speeches. Various text types will be analysed to create awareness about shifting from source culture to target culture. Comparative studies will be carried out in order to be successful in translation applications. It will be based on current culturel events and texts. Selected examples from historical literary and daily life habits will be examined.

TRIN 236.name: Group Communication and Discussion
TRIN 236.description: This course is designed to provide an understanding of group dynamics and aims to improve student communication in English and French. Emphasis will be given to verbal and nonverbal communication, active listening and responding techniques, problem solving and decision making.

TRIN 241.name: Translation of Economic and Financial Texts
TRIN 241.description: This course focuses on translation on agriculture, health, sports, and advertising. It includes translation practice on authentic texts written in one of the working languages of the students into the other. It aims to use technology well in its special fields of expertise with translation course. Translation of texts on agriculture, health, sports and advertisement with texts to be translated in their fields, it enables students to use specialized translation in their fields.

TRIN 242.name: Localisation
TRIN 242.description: Students understand the importance and the role of the translator presenting images in books or movies to the target culture and the related team work. Students can define the concept of localisation and understand translation practice into different cultural and linguistic systems. Good knowledge of technology is required for the localisation course. It will be necessary to apply many software to localisation. Students will do practical work to determine the place of the translator in localisation projects.

TRIN 265.name: Translation of Economic Texts (English-Turkish-French)
TRIN 265.description: This course consists of written translation from English into Turkish and French into Turkish on topics related to economics and business drawn from a variety of sources. The course includes terminological research and emphasizes style and language registers.

TRIN 266.name: Translation of Political and Legal Texts (English-Turkish-French)
TRIN 266.description: This course consists of written translation from English into Turkish and French into Turkish on topics related to politics and law drawn from a variety of sources. The course includes terminological research and emphasizes style and language registers.

TRIN 267.name: Sight Translation I
TRIN 267.description: This course consists of oral translation from English into Turkish and French into Turkish on texts related to economics and business. Sight translation is also used as a vehicle for voice training and enhancement of students' general knowledge.

TRIN 268.name: Sight Translation II
TRIN 268.description: This course consists of oral translation from English into Turkish and French into Turkish of texts related to politics and law. Sight translation is also used as a vehicle for voice training and enhancement of students' general knowledge.

TRIN 271.name: Business Communication
TRIN 271.description: Introduction to the theory of communication. Written and oral communication in a business environment. Emphasis is on writing business letters, business reports, participating in debates and negotiations and giving oral presentations.

TRIN 321.name: Note-Taking and Consecutive Interpretation in English
TRIN 321.description: This course aims at combining oral comprehension skills with the ability to render speeches and note them down while a speaker delivers a speech in English-Turkish language pair. Note-taking procedures and consecutive interpreting techniques will be practiced through pedagogically adapted texts.

TRIN 323.name: Note-Taking and Consecutive Interpretation in French
TRIN 323.description: This course aims at combining oral comprehension skills with the ability to render speeches and note them down while a speaker delivers a speech in the French-Turkish language pair. Note-taking procedures and consecutive interpreting techniques will be practiced through pedagogically adapted texts.

TRIN 330.name: Criticism and French Literature
TRIN 330.description: Study of a French literary work using an interdisciplinary approach. Particular emphasis will be placed on a plural reading of a novel from different aspects (historical, sociological, structural, economic, political). In addition the essential elements of the novel such as time, space, narrator, characters will be analyzed.

TRIN 332.name: Translation criticism of Anglo-American literature
TRIN 332.description: Research on translation norms and issues regarding the translation Anglo-American literature from both classic and contemporary authors across a wide variety of genres. Student led presentations of translation criticism and re-translation theory and comparative literature projects and discussions. Adaptations of literary works and the literary genre into other communicative modes such as cinema, drama and poetry.

TRIN 334.name: Media Studies
TRIN 334.description: This course provides an introduction to Media Studies. It covers all the key topics encountered in Media Studies, including images and languages, narratives, genres, representations, advertising, marketing, realisms, modernism and postmodernism, technologies, industries, institutions, independents and alternatives, and producing. The course also includes in-depth case studies and follow-up activities. Throughout the course, examples are provided from a rich range of media forms, including advertising, films, television, radio, newspapers, magazines and photography.

TRIN 335.name: Note-Taking and Consecutive Interpretation
TRIN 335.description: This course aims at combining oral comprehension with the ability to reproduce speeches and to note them down while a speaker delivers a speech. Note-taking procedures and bilateral interpretation techniques will also be stressed.

TRIN 336.name: Introduction to Simultaneous Interpretation
TRIN 336.description: This course emphasizes the techniques and practice of simultaneous interpretation. It also includes the techniques of liaison interpretation.

TRIN 337.name: Precis Writing in English-French
TRIN 337.description: This course consists of an introduction to the technique of precis-writing based on texts of a specialized nature and on recorded speeches. It also includes note-taking, editing and minute-writing.

TRIN 339.name: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication (in French)
TRIN 339.description: This course offers basic knowledge of interpersonal communication principles and their practical application in everyday interpersonal settings. Emphasis is on improving interpersonal skills and helping students increase their communication competence through readings, lectures, in-class activities and out of class assignments.

TRIN 341.name: Translation of Legal Texts
TRIN 341.description: This course concentrates on the translation of legal texts and political documents. It includes translation practices of authentic texts written in one of the working languages of the students into the other. New approaches and technology in the field will also be explored during the course.

TRIN 343.name: Translating Children's Literature
TRIN 343.description: Translating for children differs from translating for adults in a number of important ways, as the former involves more than just the translation of written content. Therefore, the course seeks to cover the procedures involved in translating for children, examine the many difficulties that arise while translating the literature for children, and the methods translators may use to overcome these difficulties.

TRIN 344.name: Diplomatic Language and Cross-Cultural Communication in Interpreting
TRIN 344.description: Diplomatic language, consecutive interpreting, bilateral interpreting, cross-cultural communication, diplomatic register, global and current affairs, coping mechanisms, performance under stress, linguistics nuances, niceties, implicatures, cultural context, diplomatic etiquette, register, ethics and code of conduct.

TRIN 346.name: Medical Terminology and Translation
TRIN 346.description: Lecture on anatomy and body systems, medical conditions and common procedures to facilitate the understanding and translation of medical texts. Research on medical terminology in Latin, Turkish and English through prefix and suffix use. Analysis of different texts to increase health literacy. Development of translation strategies for patient facing and professional facing documents based on different target groups.

TRIN 361.name: Technical Translation (English-Turkish)
TRIN 361.description: This course consists of written and oral translation from English into Turkish of scientific and technical material drawn from a variety of sources, including medical and pharmaceutical. The course includes documentary and terminological research and emphasizes style and language registers.

TRIN 363.name: Technical Translation (French-Turkish)
TRIN 363.description: This course consists of written and oral translation from French into Turkish of scientific and technical material drawn from a variety of sources, including medical and pharmaceutical. The course includes documentary and terminological research and emphasizes style and language registers.

TRIN 364.name: Literary Translation (English-Turkish)
TRIN 364.description: This course consists from English into Turkish and includes documentary and in translating literary texts from English in Turkish terminological research with emphasis on style and language registers.

TRIN 366.name: Literary Translation (French-Turkish)
TRIN 366.description: This course consists in translating literary texts from French into Turkish and includes documentary and terminological research with emphasis on style and language registers.

TRIN 373.name: Translation Profession
TRIN 373.description: This course will introduce the students to the working environments in translation, along with editing practices. Students will be able to understand how the translation processes work in the market and how translators actively participate in the process as agents with other collaborators and stakeholders.

TRIN 390.name: Summer Practice
TRIN 390.description: One month training period (20 workdays). The main objective of this period is to observe and attain experience in different work places so as to familiarize with the translation environment. Organizations may include: Translation Agencies, Estate Agencies, Media, Publishing Houses, Ministry of the EU, Ministry of the Foreign Affairs, Hotels, etc.

TRIN 406.name: Translating Arts and Culture
TRIN 406.description: This course introduces students to the critical issues that translators face in the culture and art industries, such as galleries, museums, and places for conversations about cultural heritage. The course addresses translation widely, namely, as a type of interlingual transmission and a creative platform for (re)writing texts.

TRIN 461.name: English-French Translation Workshop I
TRIN 461.description: This workshop progressively leads the student to develop French-English, English-French translation skills through intensive work on translation assignments and individual and group projects involving comparative analysis of a variety of texts.

TRIN 462.name: English-French Translation Workshop II
TRIN 462.description: This workshop further develops the students' English-French, French-English translation skills through intensive work on translation assignments and individual and group projects involving the translation of a variety of texts.

TRIN 464.name: Professional Communication for Interpreters
TRIN 464.description: The course aims to train students in the communication skills techniques required by interpreters in the professional world. Emphasis will be given to conducting meetings, negotiating contracts and presenting projects to English and French speaking audiences.

TRIN 465.name: Audiovisual Translation
TRIN 465.description: Basic concepts and the history of audiovisual translation (AVT). Assignments on the production of audiovisual texts and translations. Group projects involving the production of a wide range of audiovisual translation modes including subtitling, dubbing, voiceover, audio description and the production of remakes.

TRIN 467.name: Methodology in Translation Criticism
TRIN 467.description: Impact of linguistic choices; cultural nuances; ethical considerations on the quality of a translation; different text types and analyses (literature, business, politics, technical); analysis and critique of culturally sensitive content; translation assessment tools; translation criticism theories.

TRIN 468.name: Advanced Consecutive Interpreting
TRIN 468.description: Modes of conference interpreting; different speech types and register analysis; consecutive interpreting; simultaneous interpreting; interpreting from passive language to active languages; language augmentation; register exercises; terminology; preparation and research skills for assignments; contextual awareness; public speaking; mock conferences.

TRIN 469.name: Community Interpreting
TRIN 469.description: Community interpreting; interpreting for the courts; the police and immigration services; the medical sector in English-speaking countries and in Turkey; liaison and whispering interpreting; advanced consecutive interpreting in the English-Turkish language combination; simulations of relevant interpreting situations.

TRIN 470.name: Translation for EU and International Institutions
TRIN 470.description: Discourse and terminology of the EU; knowledge of international institutions and the EU; translation of the texts and documents produced by the European Union and other international institutions; stylistic and pragmatic linguistic features of official international texts and documents from a variety of institutions and fields; register for international organizations; proper research skills; terminology management; native choices for English-Turkish and French-Turkish language pairs.

TRIN 473.name: Advanced Turkish Communication
TRIN 473.description: Comprehensive understanding of the Turkish language, advanced use of linguistic structures, paraphrasing in Turkish for written and oral communication, grammar and syntax mastery in Turkish, cultural and contextual awareness in Turkish; advanced terminology use and proper register, stress, tone, and articulation, discourse analysis for translation purposes, exercises on breathing, diaphragm techniques, source language intervention, and mitigation techniques.

TRIN 474.name: Interpreting for Public Services
TRIN 474.description: Public service interpreting; interpreting for the courts, the police and immigration services, and the medical sector in French-speaking countries and in Turkey; liaison and whispering interpreting; advanced consecutive interpretation skills in the French-Turkish language combination; simulations of interpreting for public services; ethics and professional considerations.

TRIN 477.name: Advanced Terminology Studies
TRIN 477.description: Definition and contextual framework of terminology studies, documentation in terminological work, termbases management for specialized translation purposes, text creation and translation methods, discourse analysis on specialized texts, sustainable terminology management approaches, bilingual term extraction and management, use of AI in term extraction, terminology management software.

TRIN 480.name: Audiovisual Translation
TRIN 480.description: Audio-visual translation (AVT) modes, subtitling, dubbing, voice-over, audio description, translation strategies in audio-visual translation, translation exercises on real-world examples and projects, adaptation of written and spoken content for diverse audiovisual media, and intercultural issues in audio-visual material, quality standards, national and international professional organizations specializing in AVT.

TRIN 481.name: Consecutive and Simultaneous Interpretation Techniques
TRIN 481.description: This course provides further practice in the techniques of consecutive interpretation with emphasis on bilingual practical applications.

TRIN 484.name: Simultaneous Interpretation II: Fieldwork+Projectwork
TRIN 484.description: Practice of simultaneous interpretation. Under the supervision of a professional interpreter, the student will work in actual conference situations. Students are required to work on a project (under the supervision of an instructor) based on videotape recordings of conferences/seminars. Emphasis will be given to the preparation of dialogue lists/scripts in English/Turkish and French/Turkish and vice-versa.

TRIN 485.name: Translation workshop for EU texts and official documents
TRIN 485.description: Comparative research on the discourse and terminology used in the translation of European Union institutions texts and documents. Workshop on the research and translation techniques used in the translations of these texts from English and French into Turkish. Study of the stylistic, pragmatic, discourse aspects of official international texts and documents from a variety of institutions and fields.

TRIN 486.name: Translation project for official texts and documents
TRIN 486.description: Comparative research for translation purposes on the discourse, terminology and style used in official texts and documents of various international institutions. The design, implementation and completion of a translation project cycle individually and in groups to enhance project management and translation team skills.

TRIN 487.name: Interpreting for Public Services
TRIN 487.description: This course provides an introduction to the context of public service interpreting and stresses interpreting for the courts, the police and immigration services. Students will learn about liaison and whisper interpretation and reinforce consecutive interpretation skills all of which will be practiced through simulations of relevant interpreting situations.

TRIN 488.name: Simultaneous Interpreting
TRIN 488.description: Discourse analysis of speeches or oral texts for interpreting purposes, principles of effective communication, memory exercises, memory techniques to improve simultaneous interpreting, checking delivery during interpreting practice, paraphrasing skills, innovative restructuring, practice of SI through pedagogical and real-life speeches, real-life conference simulations, practicing preparation for assignments, developing stamina while controlling stress during the performance.

TRIN 490.name: Capstone Project
TRIN 490.description: Theoretical background, introduction to research methodologies, research ethics, potential research topics in translation and interpreting, brainstorming, assignment of research groups, developing a study design, implementing the study design in group settings, submission of research, and presentation of the research.
